headline: Revenue grows on strong demand, fuel costs squeeze margins
summary_short: Kirby reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $922.4M (+7.8% y/y, +9.3% q/q) and diluted EPS of $1.67, flat y/y but up 11% sequentially, as marine transportation revenue grew 9% y/y while segment operating margin fell to 16.4% from 20.1% on fuel-cost headwinds and elevated coastal shipyard activity.
summary_long: Total revenue rose 7.8% y/y to $922.4M as marine transportation grew 9% on strengthening inland barge utilization (low-90% range) and pricing, while distribution and services grew 6% on power-generation and commercial/industrial demand. Marine operating margin fell to 16.4% from 20.1% y/y on inland fuel-cost headwinds and elevated coastal shipyard days; distribution margin held roughly flat at 9.9%. Net income fell 4.8% y/y to $89.7M but diluted EPS was flat at $1.67 on a smaller share count after buybacks ($59.7M repurchased in Q2, $29.0M more in Q3-to-date). Cash fell to $39.0M as debt rose to fund buybacks and capex. Kirby says it expects results to trend toward the upper end of its existing 5%-15% full-year EPS growth guidance range.

drivers.explanation: Company states results reflected strong execution across both businesses, an 11% sequential EPS increase, constructive inland marine conditions, and fuel-cost/shipyard headwinds to marine margins.

Marine transportation revenue +9% y/y on strengthening inland demand and utilization and coastal revenue +10% y/y; distribution and services +6% y/y on power-generation and commercial/industrial growth.
Marine transportation operating income fell to $87.8M from $99.1M as inland fuel-cost headwinds and elevated coastal shipyard days outweighed the segment's revenue growth.
Tracks the marine segment operating-income decline described above, partly offset by 8% y/y operating-income growth in distribution and services and lower interest expense.
Flat y/y net income was offset by a smaller diluted share count (53.7M vs 56.4M y/y) from ongoing buybacks, holding EPS steady y/y and lifting it 11% q/q.
Company attributes elevated working-capital use to stronger business activity in both segments, including power-generation growth, collection/shipment timing, and higher fuel-related receivables.
Not explained in the release; the company did not state a specific cause for the q/q increase in long-term debt.
Share count fell y/y consistent with the disclosed $59.7M of Q2 share repurchases plus a further $29.0M repurchased in Q3-to-date.
